Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person who is female
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to victims
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances (NAPZA), child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of abuse and neglect. 15. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 16. Companion is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice. 18. Prosecution is the action of a public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the case and manner prescribed by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing. 19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take legal action against someone who has harmed them in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in Regional General Hospitals managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services. 21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers from perpetrators. 22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation. 23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations. 24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and their children, and mother and their children. 25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house. 26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBD is the APBD of Jember Regency. 27. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBN is the annual financial plan of the State Government approved by the House of Representatives. CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES, PURPOSES AND SERVICE PRINCIPLES

Article 2

The principles of protection of women and children victims of violence are: 1. Respect and fulfillment of victims' rights 2. Justice and gender equality

3. Non-discrimination

4. Best interests of victims

Article 3

The purpose of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and or public sphere. Article 4

The provision of services to victims is carried out with principles including free of charge, fast, safe, empathetic, non-discriminatory, easily accessible, and confidential. CHAPTER III

RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF VICTIMS

Article 5

Every victim has the right to:

1. Receive protection from the community and government as well as non-governmental institutions at the local, national and international levels. 2. Obtain information about the location of complaint centers. 3.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 17

(1) Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and or fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

(2) Appointed officials who fail to carry out obligations and responsibilities as stipulated in Article 7 shall be subject to actions and or administrative sanctions.

(3) Appointed officials who fail to carry out supervision as stipulated in Article 15 shall be subject to actions and or administrative sanctions.

(4) Actions and or administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) shall be imposed in accordance with laws and regulations.

(5) PPT managers carrying out service duties who violate service principles shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with laws and regulations.

Number 1

Number 2

Gender justice is a condition where every person both men and women are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to get opportunity (access), as well as welfare; Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Number 3

Non-Discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Number 4

The best interests of victims are all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

Article 16

(1) Guidance on the implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by the relevant Office in accordance with their respective main duties and functions.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of providing guidelines that cover the technical implementation of protection for Women and Children.

(3) Supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by the relevant office together with the Government's internal supervisory apparatus in accordance with Laws and Regulations.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men

Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur; public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur

Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 17

(1) Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and or fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

(2) Appointed officials who fail to carry out obligations and responsibilities as stipulated in Article 7 shall be subject to actions and or administrative sanctions.

(3) Appointed officials who fail to carry out supervision as stipulated in Article 15 shall be subject to actions and or administrative sanctions.

(4) Actions and or administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) shall be imposed in accordance with laws and regulations.

(5) PPT managers carrying out service duties who violate service principles shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men

Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur; public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur

Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person who is female
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to victims
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances (NAPZA), child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of abuse and neglect. 15. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 16. Companion is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice. 18. Prosecution is the action of a public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the case and manner prescribed by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing. 19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take legal action against someone who has harmed them in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in Regional General Hospitals managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services. 21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers from perpetrators. 22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation. 23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations. 24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and their children, and mother and their children. 25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house. 26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBD is the APBD of Jember Regency. 27. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBN is the annual financial plan of the State Government approved by the House of Representatives. CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES, PURPOSES AND SERVICE PRINCIPLES

Article 2

The principles of protection of women and children victims of violence are: 1. Respect and fulfillment of victims' rights 2. Justice and gender equality

3. Non-discrimination

4. Best interests of victims

Article 3

The purpose of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and or public sphere. Article 4

1. Receive protection from the community and government as well as non-governmental institutions at the local, national and international levels. 2. Obtain information about the location of complaint centers. 3.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 2

Number 1

Respect for the rights of victims is intended to guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of victims as referred to in Article 5.

Number 2

Gender justice is a condition where every person both men and women are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to get opportunity (access), as well as welfare; Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Number 3

Non-Discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Number 4

The best interests of victims are all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

Article 9

(1) The community is obligated to make efforts to provide support for the development of violence prevention programs (2) The community is obligated to prepare proposals regarding the formulation and policies on protection

(3) The community is obligated to make efforts to provide protection and moral or material support to victims

(4) The community is obligated to conduct supervision and reporting of the occurrence of acts of violence to the competent authorities.

Article 16

(1) Guidance on the implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by the relevant Office in accordance with their respective main duties and functions.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of providing guidelines that cover the technical implementation of protection for Women and Children.

(3) Supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by the relevant office together with the Government's internal supervisory apparatus in accordance with Laws and Regulations.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men

Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur; public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur

Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

CONCERNING

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN JEMBER REGENCY

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 16

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of providing guidelines that cover the technical implementation of protection for Women and Children.

(3) Supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by the relevant office together with the Government's internal supervisory apparatus in accordance with Laws and Regulations.

(1) Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and or fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

(2) Appointed officials who fail to carry out obligations and responsibilities as stipulated in Article 7 shall be subject to actions and or administrative sanctions.

Number 1

Number 2

Gender justice is a condition where every person both men and women are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to get opportunity (access), as well as welfare; Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Number 3

Non-Discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Number 4

The best interests of victims are all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

Article 9

(1) The community is obligated to make efforts to provide support for the development of violence prevention programs (2) The community is obligated to prepare proposals regarding the formulation and policies on protection

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration

4. Woman is a person who is female
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to victims
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 12. 13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. 20. Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life

Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 10. I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration

6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person who is female
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to victims
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances (NAPZA), child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of abuse and neglect. 15. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 16. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice. 18. Prosecution is the action of a public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the case and manner prescribed by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing. 19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take legal action against someone who has harmed them in a civil manner
20. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation. 23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations. 24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and their children, and mother and their children. 25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house. 26. Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person who is female
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to victims
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances (NAPZA), child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of abuse and neglect. 15. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 16. Companion is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice. 18. Prosecution is the action of a public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the case and manner prescribed by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing. 19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take legal action against someone who has harmed them in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in Regional General Hospitals managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services. 21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers from perpetrators. 22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation. 23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations. 24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and their children, and mother and their children. 25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house. 26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBD is the APBD of Jember Regency. 27. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBN is the annual financial plan of the State Government approved by the House of Representatives. CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES, PURPOSES AND SERVICE PRINCIPLES

Article 2

The principles of protection of women and children victims of violence are: 1. Respect and fulfillment of victims' rights 2. Justice and gender equality

3. Non-discrimination

4. Best interests of victims

Article 3

The purpose of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and or public sphere. Article 4

The provision of services to victims is carried out with principles including free of charge, fast, safe, empathetic, non-discriminatory, easily accessible, and confidential. CHAPTER III

RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF VICTIMS

Article 5

Every victim has the right to:

1. Receive protection from the community and government as well as non-governmental institutions at the local, national and international levels. 2. Obtain information about the location of complaint centers. 3.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN JEMBER REGENCY

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN JEMBER REGENCY

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 10. I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person who is female
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to victims
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances (NAPZA), child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of abuse and neglect. 15. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations. 24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and their children, and mother and their children. 25. I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of providing guidelines that cover the technical implementation of protection for Women and Children.

(3) Supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by the relevant office together with the Government's internal supervisory apparatus in accordance with Laws and Regulations.

Article 2

Number 1

Respect for the rights of victims is intended to guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of victims as referred to in Article 5.

Number 2

Gender justice is a condition where every person both men and women are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to get opportunity (access), as well as welfare; Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Number 3

Non-Discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Number 4

The best interests of victims are all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically. 8. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 12. 13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. 20. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations. 24. I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all the blood of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution on Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty and thus must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.
